seasonStatusMeaning.peak: Heaviest harvest, lowest prices, glut in the market
seasonStatusMeaning.inSeason: Good supply — the produce is actively selling
seasonStatusMeaning.offSeason: Scarce, stored or imported stock — highest prices

produce.name: Tomatoes
produce.description: Nigeria's most traded vegetable. Sold by the basket from northern irrigation belts and southern farms; prices swing hardest of any produce when supply thins.
produce.nutrition: Rich in lycopene, vitamin C and potassium. Cooking with oil raises lycopene absorption.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Pick firm fruit with a deep, even colour and tight skin. Reject soft patches, splits and any fruit leaking juice — one spoiled tomato spreads rot through the basket.
optional.optimalStorage: Store at room temperature, stem-side down, never refrigerate whole; keep out of direct sun and use within 3-5 days. Green fruit ripens off the vine.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Rich in lycopene, vitamin C and potassium. Cooking with oil raises lycopene absorption.

produce.name: Pepper (Chilli / Tatase)
produce.description: Fresh red and green chilli, plus the milder tatase. Sold by the basket and used in nearly every Nigerian soup and stew base.
produce.nutrition: High in vitamin C — weight for weight, more than citrus — plus capsaicin, an anti-inflammatory compound.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Choose glossy, firm pods with intact stalks. Wrinkled skin signals age; black soft spots mean it will not survive the trip home.
optional.optimalStorage: Sun-dry or smoke to extend shelf life for months; fresh pods keep 1-2 weeks in a breathable sack in a cool, dry room.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: High in vitamin C — weight for weight, more than citrus — plus capsaicin, an anti-inflammatory compound.

produce.name: Yam
produce.description: The premium tuber, sold by the hundred. New yam arrives with the harvest festivals; old yam holds through the dry season.
produce.nutrition: A major carbohydrate source, high in potassium and resistant starch; lower glycaemic load than white rice.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Judge by weight and sound — a good tuber is heavy for its size and rings solid when tapped. Avoid soft ends, sprouting eyes and dark surface lesions.
optional.optimalStorage: Store tubers upright in a dark, ventilated barn or rack, never stacked flat on bare floor; a dry, airy store holds yam for 3-6 months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: A major carbohydrate source, high in potassium and resistant starch; lower glycaemic load than white rice.

produce.name: Beans (Cowpea)
produce.description: Dried cowpea sold by the bag, the country's main plant protein and the base of moi moi and akara.
produce.nutrition: Excellent plant protein and fibre, plus iron and folate; soaking before cooking reduces the flatulence compounds.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Shake the bag — loose dust means weevil damage. Grain should be uniform, hard and free of holes; press a handful, it should not crumble.
optional.optimalStorage: Store dry in an airtight drum or double-bagged sack with a little dried pepper or ash to deter weevils; keeps 6-12 months if kept bone dry.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Excellent plant protein and fibre, plus iron and folate; soaking before cooking reduces the flatulence compounds.

produce.name: Rice
produce.description: Local parboiled rice sold in 50kg bags, from the Kebbi, Ebonyi and Niger river basins.
produce.nutrition: Main energy staple; local parboiled rice retains more B vitamins than fully polished white rice.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Look for whole, translucent grains with few broken pieces. Musty smell or yellowing indicates poor drying or old stock.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep in a dry, airtight container off the floor; a dry store holds milled rice for a year, but humid storage invites mould fast.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Main energy staple; local parboiled rice retains more B vitamins than fully polished white rice.

produce.name: Onions
produce.description: Sold in 100kg bags, mostly from Sokoto and Kebbi. A dry-season staple that stores for months with the right handling.
produce.nutrition: Contains quercetin and organosulphur compounds; a useful source of vitamin C and fibre.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Firm bulbs with dry, papery skins and no green shoots. A soft neck or a damp base means it is already spoiling.
optional.optimalStorage: Cure in shade for two weeks, then store in a net or slatted crate with airflow. Never seal in polythene — trapped moisture rots the whole lot.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Contains quercetin and organosulphur compounds; a useful source of vitamin C and fibre.

produce.name: Cassava
produce.description: Fresh roots sold by the hundred and processed almost immediately into garri, fufu and chips.
produce.nutrition: High in carbohydrate and vitamin C; must always be properly processed, as raw cassava contains cyanogenic compounds.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Choose hard, heavy roots with intact skin. A soft, waxy feel or blue-black streaks means the root has begun to rot.
optional.optimalStorage: Roots spoil within 48 hours of harvest — process into garri, fufu or chips immediately. Store processed garri dry in sacks for months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: High in carbohydrate and vitamin C; must always be properly processed, as raw cassava contains cyanogenic compounds.

produce.name: Plantain
produce.description: Sold by the bunch, unripe for frying and ripe for boiling. A year-round staple with a sharp seasonal price curve.
produce.nutrition: Rich in potassium, vitamin A and fiber. Lower glycemic index than ripe bananas.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Pick by intended use — green and hard for frying, yellow with black speckles for boiling and roasting. Reject bruised or mouldy tips.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep at room temperature and let it ripen naturally; refrigeration halts ripening and turns the flesh grey. Ripening can be slowed by separating the fingers.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Good source of potassium, vitamin B6 and resistant starch when green.

produce.name: Garri
produce.description: Fermented cassava grits in 50kg bags, the most widely stored staple food in the south.
produce.nutrition: Fermented cassava product, energy-dense and low in fat; pair with protein-rich soup to balance the meal.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Fine, dry and evenly coloured, with no sour or mouldy smell. Squeeze a handful — it should sift, not clump.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep in an airtight container in a dry room; moisture turns garri sour within weeks. A dry sack holds good quality for 6 months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Fermented cassava product, energy-dense and low in fat; pair with protein-rich soup to balance the meal.

produce.name: Millet
produce.description: Drought-tolerant grain sold by the bag, milled into flour for porridge and local drinks.
produce.nutrition: High in fibre, B vitamins and minerals like iron and magnesium. Gluten-free and easily digestible.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Look for small, uniform, golden grains with no dust or grit. A bitter taste after milling may mean poor cleaning.
optional.optimalStorage: Extremely drought-tolerant grain that also stores well — keep dry and airtight in a cool room for up to a year.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Gluten-free, high in magnesium and iron; a low-glycaemic grain suited to diabetic diets.

produce.name: Maize
produce.description: Sold dry in 100kg bags and fresh on the cob in season, the country's core cereal.
produce.nutrition: Rich in carbohydrates, B vitamins and fibre. Contains lutein and zeaxanthin for eye health.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Grain should be hard, bright and free of mould. A musty or sour smell is a serious quality failure — do not buy it.
optional.optimalStorage: Dry to below 13% moisture before bagging, then store with an approved grain protectant; damp grain develops aflatoxin quickly.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Energy staple rich in B vitamins and lutein; nixtamalisation or fermentation improves nutrient availability.

produce.name: Sorghum (Guinea Corn)
produce.description: Guinea corn, sold by the bag for flour, pap and traditional brewing.
produce.nutrition: High in fibre, protein and antioxidants. Gluten-free and good for heart health.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Uniform red-brown grain, hard and free from mould. Reject any grain with a pink or dark discolouration.
optional.optimalStorage: Store dry and airtight; sorghum holds 8-12 months in a cool, low-humidity store.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Gluten-free and rich in antioxidants; traditionally brewed into local drinks and porridges.

produce.name: Groundnuts
produce.description: Sold shelled by the bag and pressed for oil; a major northern cash crop.
produce.nutrition: Excellent source of plant protein, healthy fats, vitamin E and magnesium. Good for heart health.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Choose well-filled, rattling shells and clean, unpitted kernels. Dry, blackened or bitter kernels must be discarded.
optional.optimalStorage: Store shelled nuts in a dry, cool place — never damp, as aflatoxin risk rises sharply with moisture. Airtight drums hold quality for 6 months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Protein, healthy fats, vitamin E and magnesium; a valuable oilseed as well as a snack.

produce.name: Fresh Fish
produce.description: Sold fresh by the kilogram from ponds, rivers and coastal landings.
produce.nutrition: Lean protein, omega-3 fatty acids and iodine; a key micronutrient source for growing children.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Bright, bulging eyes, red gills, firm springy flesh and a clean sea smell. Sunken eyes or a slimy surface mean it is past its best.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep on ice from purchase to kitchen; rinse in clean water and cook or smoke within 24 hours. Never refreeze thawed fish.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Lean protein, omega-3 fatty acids and iodine; a key micronutrient source for growing children.

produce.name: Banana
produce.description: Sweet eating banana sold by the bunch alongside plantain in southern markets.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Plump, evenly coloured fruit, firm but yielding to gentle pressure, with intact stems and no dark bruising.
optional.optimalStorage: Ripen at room temperature, then refrigerate for 2-3 days to hold sweetness; the skin darkens in cold but the flesh stays good.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Potassium, vitamin B6 and vitamin C; sugar content rises sharply as the fruit ripens.

produce.name: Smoked / Dried Fish
produce.description: Kiln-smoked and dried fish sold by the kilogram — the preserved protein that travels to inland markets.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Dry but slightly flexible, amber colour, smoky aroma, no white mould or insect holes.
optional.optimalStorage: Store in a dry, ventilated basket or hang in a cool smokehouse; keeps weeks to months but must never be stacked while warm.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Concentrated protein and calcium — especially if eaten with bones — plus long-chain omega-3s.

produce.name: Sweet Potatoes
produce.description: Orange and white-fleshed roots sold by the hundred, rich in vitamin A.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Smooth, firm roots free of cuts or sprouting. Soft ends or black spots mean rot has started.
optional.optimalStorage: Cure for a week in a warm humid space, then store cool and dark; never refrigerate raw roots, which turns them hard and bitter.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Very high in beta-carotene (orange varieties) and vitamin A — important for children's diets.

produce.name: Okra
produce.description: Tender pods sold by the basket, the thickening agent in Nigerian soups.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Small, firm, snap-crisp pods with no browning at the tips — large dull pods are woody.
optional.optimalStorage: Use within 2-3 days; a dry cloth bag in the coolest part of the kitchen slows the softening. Do not wash until cooking.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Rich in mucilage and folate; the pods are a good source of vitamin K and fibre.

produce.name: Ugu (Pumpkin Leaf)
produce.description: Fluted pumpkin leaf sold in bundles, the most used leafy vegetable in southern cooking.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Deep green, unblemished leaves with crisp stems. Yellowing or wilting means they were cut too long ago.
optional.optimalStorage: Wrap in a slightly damp cloth in the fridge for up to 4 days; blanching and drying holds them for months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: High in beta-carotene, vitamin C and iron; the seeds are traditionally used as a vermifuge.

produce.name: Waterleaf
produce.description: Soft, watery leaf sold in bundles and cooked within a day or two of harvest.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Tender, glossy, deep-green leaves on thin stems; the leaf should feel moist, not slimy.
optional.optimalStorage: Very perishable — use within a day or two. Wrap in a damp cloth in the fridge, or blanch and freeze.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Hydrating and a good source of vitamin C, calcium and iron.

produce.name: Soybeans
produce.description: Sold by the bag for oil, flour and livestock feed.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Uniform, cream-coloured, hard beans free of splits and mould. Reject any with a musty smell.
optional.optimalStorage: Store dry and airtight; soy keeps well for 9-12 months in a cool, low-humidity store.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Complete plant protein, plus isoflavones and healthy polyunsaturated fats.

produce.name: Crayfish
produce.description: Dried and ground crayfish sold by the kilogram as a soup flavour base.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Dry, pinkish-orange, crumbly with a strong savoury aroma. Off-white colour or a musty smell means age.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep in an airtight jar away from moisture; dry, ground crayfish holds for months if it stays dry.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Concentrated protein, calcium and iodine; used as a flavour base across Nigerian soups.

produce.name: Bitter Leaf
produce.description: Sold in bundles and washed to temper its bitterness; central to bitterleaf soup.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Fresh, bright green leaves with a crisp snap. Limp or yellow leaves have lost most of their bitterness and nutrients.
optional.optimalStorage: Use fresh within 3 days, or wash, squeeze and freeze in portions for months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Bitter compounds with traditional medicinal use; a source of vitamin C, iron and zinc.

produce.name: Palm Oil
produce.description: Unrefined red palm oil sold by the keg, the base fat of southern cooking.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Deep red-orange colour, clean smell, no sediment layer. A pale or cloudy oil has been diluted or poorly processed.
optional.optimalStorage: Store in a cool, dark place in a sealed container; unrefined red palm oil keeps about 6 months before flavour fades.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Rich in vitamin A precursors and vitamin E; high in saturated fat, so use in moderation.

produce.name: Groundnut Oil
produce.description: Clear, pale-gold cooking oil pressed from groundnut, sold by the keg.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Clear, pale gold, with a mild nutty smell. Cloudiness or a rancid smell means heat damage.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep sealed, cool and out of light; a good groundnut oil holds 6-12 months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: High in monounsaturated fat and vitamin E; suited to high-heat frying.

produce.name: Wheat
produce.description: Sold by the bag for flour milling, grown under irrigation in the north.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Plump, uniform amber grain, free of stones, chaff and mould.
optional.optimalStorage: Store dry and airtight, protected from rodents; a cool dry room holds it 10-12 months.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Gluten-containing grain, high in protein and B vitamins when whole.

produce.name: Sesame Seed
produce.description: Beniseed sold by the bag; a major export crop and oil source.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Clean, uniformly creamy-white seed with no sand or grit; it should pour freely.
optional.optimalStorage: Keep dry and airtight; sesame keeps up to a year and is highly resistant to insects.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Rich in calcium, magnesium and healthy fats; a major Nigerian export crop.

produce.name: Amaranth (Tete)
produce.description: Tender amaranth leaf sold in bundles, a fast-growing green used in soups and as a weaning food.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Tender leaves and soft stems, deep green with no flower buds, which signal toughness.
optional.optimalStorage: Cook within 2-3 days; wrap in a damp cloth and refrigerate, or blanch and freeze.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: High in iron, calcium and beta-carotene; a traditional weaning food.

produce.name: Ginger
produce.description: Fresh and dried rhizomes sold by the kilogram, grown mainly on the Kaduna and Plateau highlands.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Firm, heavy rhizomes with tight, unwrinkled skin and a clean fresh smell. Soft or mouldy fingers should be rejected.
optional.optimalStorage: Fresh rhizomes keep weeks in a dry, airy spot; dried and ground, ginger holds for a year.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Gingerol compounds aid digestion and nausea; strong antioxidant content.

produce.name: Turmeric
produce.description: Bright orange rhizomes and powder sold by the kilogram, a smaller highland crop beside ginger.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Firm rhizomes with vivid orange flesh when cut. Pale or dry flesh indicates poor quality.
optional.optimalStorage: Fresh rhizomes keep for weeks when dry; powder keeps a year stored dark and airtight.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Curcumin is a potent anti-inflammatory; best absorbed with black pepper and fat.

produce.name: Irish Potatoes
produce.description: Temperate potato sold by the bag and grown almost entirely on the Plateau and Mambilla highlands.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Firm, smooth, unblemished tubers with no sprouts. Green skin or a soft feel must be rejected.
optional.optimalStorage: Store dark, cool and ventilated, never in light — greening makes the tuber toxic. Airtight plastic encourages rot.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Good source of vitamin C and potassium; glycaemic impact drops when cooled after cooking.

produce.name: Carrots
produce.description: Sold by the bag from northern irrigation schemes, a cool-season crop.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Bright orange, firm, evenly tapered roots with no cracks or fork branching; larger is not better.
optional.optimalStorage: Trim the tops and refrigerate in a perforated bag for weeks; cool humid storage is essential.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Very high in beta-carotene; cooking with fat improves absorption.

produce.name: Cabbage
produce.description: Tight heads sold by the head, grown on the highlands around Jos.
produce.seasonNote: Nigerian harvest pattern; northern irrigated belts extend tomato, onion and carrot availability into the dry season.

optional.selectAtMarket: Tight, heavy, compact heads with crisp outer leaves. Loose or puffy heads are past their peak.
optional.optimalStorage: Refrigerate whole for up to two weeks; once cut, wrap tightly and use within days.
optional.nutritionalHighlight: Vitamin C, vitamin K and glucosinolate compounds; low in calories.
